questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue (Poisson batch arrivals at rate $\lambda_B$, i.i.d. batch sizes $B$, i.i.d. $\operatorname{Exp}(\mu)$ job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]$, one server, each batch moves to the server as a whole), which time does the waiting time $W$ of a job measure?
options: The time from the job's arrival until it starts its own service.
The time from the job's arrival until its batch reaches the server.
The time from the job's arrival until it leaves the system.
The time from the job's arrival until its whole batch has been served.

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue (Poisson batch arrivals at rate $\lambda_B$, i.i.d. batch sizes $B$, i.i.d. $\operatorname{Exp}(\mu)$ job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]$, one server, each batch moves to the server as a whole) with load $\rho=\lambda_B\mathbb{E}[B]\mathbb{E}[S]<1$, why is the extra assumption $\mathbb{E}[B^2]<\infty$ needed for the mean waiting time formula?
options: It guarantees that arriving batches see time averages of the queue.
It is needed for the load $\rho$ to be finite and below one.
The mean number of jobs at the server involves $\mathbb{E}[B^2]$.
It makes the individual job arrivals form a Poisson process.

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue (Poisson batch arrivals at rate $\lambda_B$, i.i.d. batch sizes $B$, i.i.d. $\operatorname{Exp}(\mu)$ job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]$, one server, each batch moves to the server as a whole), an arriving batch finds $L_s^B$ jobs of the batch at the server and $Q^B$ batches in queue. Which quantity is $\mathbb{E}[L_s^B]+\mathbb{E}[Q^B]\,\mathbb{E}[B]$?
options: The mean number of jobs in the system seen by an arriving batch.
The mean number of batches in the system seen by an arriving batch.
The mean number of jobs in queue, not counting the server.
The mean number of jobs that arrive while a batch is waiting.

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue (Poisson batch arrivals at rate $\lambda_B$, i.i.d. batch sizes $B$, i.i.d. $\operatorname{Exp}(\mu)$ job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]$, one server, each batch moves to the server as a whole), the batch-size distribution is made more variable while $\lambda_B$, $\mathbb{E}[B]$ and $\mathbb{E}[S]$ stay fixed. How does the mean waiting time $\mathbb{E}[W]$ change?
options: It stays the same, because the load $\rho$ and $\mathbb{E}[B]$ do not change.
It decreases, because small batches now reach the server more quickly.
It increases only through $\rho$, which grows with the batch-size variance.
It increases, because the factor $(1+C_B^2)/2$ grows while $\rho$ is fixed.

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue (Poisson batch arrivals at rate $\lambda_B$, i.i.d. batch sizes $B$, i.i.d. $\operatorname{Exp}(\mu)$ job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]$, one server, each batch moves to the server as a whole), every batch contains exactly $b\ge2$ jobs, so $C_B^2=0$. With $\rho=\lambda_Bb\,\mathbb{E}[S]$, which expression is the mean waiting time $\mathbb{E}[W]$?
options: $\dfrac{\rho}{1-\rho}\,\mathbb{E}[S]$
$b\,\dfrac{\rho}{1-\rho}\,\mathbb{E}[S]$
$\dfrac{b+1}{2}\,\dfrac{\rho}{1-\rho}\,\mathbb{E}[S]$
$\dfrac{b}{2}\,\dfrac{\rho}{1-\rho}\,\mathbb{E}[S]$

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1$ queue with exponential job service times has batches arriving at rate $\lambda_B=2$ per hour, each batch containing exactly $2$ jobs, mean job service time $\mathbb{E}[S]=10$ minutes and mean number of jobs in the system $\mathbb{E}[L]=3$. What is the mean waiting time $\mathbb{E}[W]$ of a job?
options: $90$ minutes
$30$ minutes
$45$ minutes
$60$ minutes

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue a batch of $4$ jobs reaches the server and its jobs have service times $5$, $8$, $2$ and $6$ minutes, served in this order. What is the area $Z$ under the number of jobs of this batch at the server, in job-minutes?

The batch size $B$ of an $M^B/M/1$ queue has $\mathbb{E}[B]=3$ and $\mathbb{E}[B^2]=12$. What is its squared coefficient of variation $C_B^2=\operatorname{Var}(B)/(\mathbb{E}[B])^2$, which enters the mean waiting-time formula?

An $M^B/M/1$ queue has First Success batch sizes, $\mathbb{P}(B=k)=(1-p)^{k-1}p$ for $k\ge1$, with $p=1/4$, exponential job service times and load $\rho=0.6$. What is the mean number of jobs $\mathbb{E}[L]$ in the system?

An $M^B/M/1$ queue has every batch consisting of a single job ($B\equiv1$), load $\rho=0.5$ and mean job service time $\mathbb{E}[S]=4$ minutes. What does the batch-arrival formula give for the mean waiting time $\mathbb{E}[W]$?
options: $2$ minutes
$4$ minutes
$8$ minutes
$1$ minute

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue with batch rate $\lambda_B$ and load $\rho=\lambda_B\mathbb{E}[B]\mathbb{E}[S]$, a batch's mean waiting time satisfies $\mathbb{E}[W^B]=(\mathbb{E}[L_s^B]+\mathbb{E}[Q^B]\mathbb{E}[B])\mathbb{E}[S]$, with $L_s^B$ jobs at the server and $Q^B$ queued batches. Using Little's law $\mathbb{E}[Q^B]=\lambda_B\mathbb{E}[W^B]$, what is $\mathbb{E}[W^B]$?
options: $\dfrac{\mathbb{E}[L_s^B]\,\mathbb{E}[S]}{1-\lambda_B\mathbb{E}[S]}$
$\dfrac{\mathbb{E}[L_s^B]\,\mathbb{E}[S]}{1+\rho}$
$\dfrac{\mathbb{E}[B]\,\mathbb{E}[L_s^B]\,\mathbb{E}[S]}{1-\rho}$
$\dfrac{\mathbb{E}[L_s^B]\,\mathbb{E}[S]}{1-\rho}$

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue (Poisson batches at rate $\lambda_B$, i.i.d. batch sizes $B$, exponential job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]$, batches served whole in arrival order), the mean batch size $\mathbb{E}[B]$ is doubled while $C_B^2$, $\mathbb{E}[S]$ and the load $\rho\in(0,1)$ are kept fixed by halving $\lambda_B$. How does the mean waiting time $\mathbb{E}[W]$ change?
options: It increases, but by less than a factor of two.
It doubles exactly, since it is proportional to $\mathbb{E}[B]$.
It stays the same, because the load $\rho$ is unchanged.
It increases by a factor of four, through $\mathbb{E}[B^2]$.

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue (Poisson batches at rate $\lambda_B$, i.i.d. batch sizes $B$, exponential job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]$, batches served whole in arrival order, load $\rho=\lambda_B\mathbb{E}[B]\mathbb{E}[S]<1$), $Z_k$ is the area under the number $L_s^B$ of jobs of batch $k$ at the server during that batch's service, with $\mathbb{E}[Z_k]=\mathbb{E}[B(B+1)/2]\,\mathbb{E}[S]$. Which expression does the renewal reward theorem give for the time average $\mathbb{E}[L_s^B]$?
options: $\lambda_B\,\mathbb{E}[B]\,\mathbb{E}[Z_k]$
$\mathbb{E}[Z_k]/(\mathbb{E}[B]\,\mathbb{E}[S])$
$\lambda_B\,\mathbb{E}[Z_k]$
$\mathbb{E}[Z_k]/\lambda_B$

questions.question: Two single-server queues have Poisson batch arrivals at rate $\lambda_B=2$ per hour, exponential job service times and batches served whole in arrival order. In queue S every batch is a single job with mean service time $15$ minutes; in queue P every batch consists of exactly $2$ jobs, each with mean service time $7.5$ minutes, so both queues have load $\rho=0.5$. By how many minutes does the mean waiting time $\mathbb{E}[W_S]$ of a job in queue S exceed the mean waiting time $\mathbb{E}[W_P]$ of a job in queue P (a negative value means the jobs in P wait longer)?
options: $0$ minutes
$3.75$ minutes
$7.5$ minutes
$-7.5$ minutes

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1$ queue has batches arriving at rate $\lambda_B=1$ per hour, batch size $B=1$ or $B=3$ with probability $1/2$ each, and exponential job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]=12$ minutes. What is the mean waiting time $\mathbb{E}[W]$ of a job?
options: $12$ minutes
$16$ minutes
$9$ minutes
$14$ minutes

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1$ queue has batches arriving at rate $\lambda_B=4$ per hour with mean batch size $\mathbb{E}[B]=3$, and the mean waiting time of a job is $\mathbb{E}[W]=30$ minutes. What is the mean number of jobs that belong to batches waiting in the queue, $\mathbb{E}[Q^B]\,\mathbb{E}[B]$?

In a single-server queue with Poisson batch arrivals, batches served in order of arrival and each batch moved to the server as a whole, the job service times are changed from exponential to deterministic with the same mean $\mathbb{E}[S]$. Does $\mathbb{E}[W]=\mathbb{E}[L]\,\mathbb{E}[S]$ still hold, with $W$ a job's time until its batch reaches the server and $L$ the number of jobs in the system?
options: Yes, because PASTA still lets arriving batches see time averages.
Yes, because Little's law holds for any service-time distribution.
No, the job in service no longer needs $\mathbb{E}[S]$ on average.
No, because the batches no longer arrive as a Poisson process.

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1$ queue (Poisson batches, exponential job service times, batches served whole in arrival order), $W$ is a job's time until its batch reaches the server and $W^B$ a batch's waiting time. Which statement relating the job average $\mathbb{E}[W]$ to the batch average $\mathbb{E}[W^B]$ is correct?
options: $\mathbb{E}[W]=\mathbb{E}[W^B]$ only for fixed batch sizes, since otherwise large batches weigh more.
$\mathbb{E}[W]=\mathbb{E}[W^B]/\mathbb{E}[B]$, since a batch's wait is shared among its jobs.
$\mathbb{E}[W]>\mathbb{E}[W^B]$, since jobs tend to be in large batches, which wait longer.
$\mathbb{E}[W]=\mathbb{E}[W^B]$, since a batch's wait does not depend on its own size.

questions.question: Two $M^B/M/1$ queues have the same job rate, the same exponential job service times and load $\rho=0.75$. Queue G has First Success batches, $\mathbb{P}(B=k)=(2/3)^{k-1}(1/3)$ for $k\ge1$; queue F has fixed batches $B\equiv3$. What is the ratio $\mathbb{E}[W_G]/\mathbb{E}[W_F]$ of their mean waiting times?

An $M^B/M/1$ queue has batches arriving at rate $\lambda_B=1$ per hour, batch size $B=1$ with probability $2/3$ and $B=4$ with probability $1/3$, and exponential job service times with mean $\mathbb{E}[S]=0.2$ hour. What is the mean number of jobs of the batch at the server, $\mathbb{E}[L_s^B]$?
